name: sync_basic
kind: installation from the version 1 / 2 readings, frozen before any replay with the changed engine; no new GPU data: (R1) a warp's own completed phase carries no release latency, (R2) the mbarrier SYNCS instructions of an SM are served one at a time, (R3) nanosleep follows the measured requests. The hand-off between two warps and bar.sync are NOT installed here (version 4 measures what is missing)
why: Versions 1 and 2 left four disagreements between replay and hardware. Re-reading their tables instruction by instruction (below) shows that two of them rest on data that is complete (the warp's own phase, the per-SM service; plus nanosleep) and two do not (the hand-off between warps, bar.sync). This version installs the first group and says why the second waits.
data_seen_before_freezing: sync_basic v1 / v2 addenda and derive tables ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/sync_basic{,-v2}/derive-<device>.txt), the 74ce8aab replays in them, the leaves synchronization.mbarrier.release, instruction.service SYNCS.PHASECHK, control.nanosleep and their source records (barrier_release, trywait_wake, nanosleep), and a static census of NANOSLEEP in the full-GPU captures. No replay with a changed engine.

(a) Sample totals. Summed over the loop-body pcs and classes, the hardware samples give cycles per iteration with no frame constant (the clock columns carry a per-cell constant of 4-8 cycles per iteration from the code between the clock reads and the loop, so 'clock minus s.loop' is uncertain by 1-4). arrive + try_wait of the same warp, warps per CTA 1 / 2 / 4 / 8: h100 27.68 / 32.96 / 47.24 / 86.87, b300 27.24 / 31.27 / 49.92 / 85.96; every lane arriving, 1 / 4 warps: 27.99 / 51.09 and 27.56 / 50.95. Of that, long_scoreboard on the readers of the try_wait: h100 16.96 / 22.24 / 36.16 / 42.65 (+ mio_throttle 32.67 on the SYNCS at 8 warps), b300 17.03 / 20.92 / 38.92 / 53.76 (+ 21.97). Replay 74ce8aab: 101.9 at every shape, 83.5 of it semantic:mbarrier_wait on the try_wait.

(b) The one-warp cell is explained by the installed result latency alone. The unrolled trip holds four pairs with two try_waits in flight; if each try_wait returns L cycles after its issue and nothing else waits, the readers wait 2L - 8 cycles per trip; with the installed SYNCS.PHASECHK result latency (37.93 / 37.92) that is 16.96 per iteration, the measured 16.96 (h100) and 17.03 (b300). So the uncontended latency is already right and the replay's error is the release latency (87.9) it puts on the warp's own completed phase.

(c) Service. From 4 warps on the iteration grows by about 10 cycles per warp of the SM (two SYNCS per warp), independent of SMSP and of the number of arriving lanes: one server per SM at 5.4-6.4 cycles per SYNCS instruction. Pencil check (tools/microbench/sync_basic/service_toy.py: FIFO server, latency 37.93 from service start, no engine): interval 5.67 gives 27.1 / 31.6 / 45.4 / 90.7 for 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 warps against h100 27.68 / 32.96 / 47.24 / 86.87 and b300 27.24 / 31.27 / 49.92 / 85.96: within 6 % except b300 at 4 warps (-9 %; every-lane cells -11 %). One interval cannot give 4 and 8 warps exactly (per SYNCS 5.9-6.4 at 4 warps, 5.4 at 8); the hardware also books part of the wait at 8 warps on the SYNCS instructions as mio_throttle (a bounded queue), which this rule does not model (queue depth belongs to the MIO step).

(d) CORRECTION of the version 2 hand-off reading. The ping-pong period is not two hand-offs. Per pc (h100, cycles per execution): member 1 sits about 50 cycles at its try_wait before issuing it (branch_resolving 42: the YIELD ptxas places in front of the try_wait, cf. 33.4 per NOP after yield + stall 0 in warp_issue), then 37 on the reader, which is the plain result latency: its try_wait is issued after the other warp's arrive and does not block. Member 0's try_wait blocks (97 on the reader). The period (137) is member 1's own loop, and member 0 has slack; all the cell says about the hand-off (arrive issue -> the blocked waiter's reader issues) is an upper bound of about 42 cycles for a waiter that had been blocked about 60 cycles. The '65-67 cycles per hand-off' of the version 2 addendum is half a period with the YIELD and the branches in it, not a latency. The compiled-probe values (barrier_release 87.9: same-thread chain; trywait_wake 228 / 146: poll loop with YIELD and 64-bit clock reads, the spinning control alone 174 / 156) do not isolate it either. The hand-off is therefore not known and nothing about another warp's wait is changed here.

(e) bar.sync. Sample totals minus the loop frame, all warps arriving together: 9.5 / 15.6 / 39.0 cycles per barrier at 1 / 4 / 16 warps on both devices (2 and 8 warps have clocks only: about 11.5 / 23.5) = 7.5 + 2.0 per warp. The installed 16.0 came from barrier_release 'warplast' (the last warp arriving late), flat over 4-16 warps. One-at-a-time service of arrivals (2 cycles each) fits both, a release latency that grows with the participant count fits only the new cells; the late-arrival case has not been measured in a hand-written kernel. Not installed here.

(f) nanosleep. The converter supplies the request in ns under the axis name requested_sleep_cycles, while the installed leaf (12083 + 1.044 x, nanosleep v2) was fitted over ns x clock: every replayed sleep is 12083 + 1.044 x ns (12187 for 100 ns, 22523 for 10 us; the replays in the version 1 / 2 tables). Static census of plain NANOSLEEP in the two full-GPU capture sets: requests of 100-1030 ns only (0x64, 0x100, 0x15e, 0x1c2, 0x406 and register forms); NANOSLEEP.SYNCS (10 ms and 50 us hints) is the suspended try_wait, a different path, not touched.

rules.R1: Own phase. When the arrive that completes a phase of an mbarrier object is issued by warp X (an mbarrier_arrive row of an instruction whose operation class begins with SYNCS; not a transaction completion), a wait on that phase issued by warp X itself (an mbarrier_wait row that is not a known failed poll and has no deferred block) is ready as soon as the phase is complete in the object's state: synchronization.mbarrier.release.cycles, suspended_wake_cycles and the store-visibility settle are not applied to it. The wait then issues and its result takes the SYNCS.PHASECHK result latency as before. Waits by any other warp, deferred blocks, failed polls and NANOSLEEP.SYNCS are unchanged.
rules.R2: Service. Each SM has one server for the SYNCS instructions that carry an mbarrier_arrive or mbarrier_wait row (operation class beginning with SYNCS; known failed polls take no turn). In issue order: service_start = max(issue cycle, server_free); server_free = service_start + service_interval_cycles. An arrive's effects are dated at its service_start (the phase completion cycle and everything derived from it); a wait's result latency counts from its service_start. Issue itself is never delayed by the server. service_interval_cycles is a new field of synchronization.mbarrier.release (cycles, scope SM, cluster-local); 0 or absent = no server and the previous timing bit for bit.
rules.R3: nanosleep. control.nanosleep.cycles becomes a piecewise-linear table over the request as the converter supplies it (ns), with the measured points below; the engine rule is unchanged (wake = issue + cycles, PTX cap 1 ms, NANOSLEEP.SYNCS and syncs_wake_cycles untouched). The axis keeps its name in this version; renaming it (requested_sleep_ns) goes with the pending pure-refactor clean-up so that this commit changes no job content besides the leaf.

leaves.synchronization.mbarrier.release.service: s = sum_i(T_i k_i) / sum_i(k_i^2) over the cells in which the server is saturated (s.mbar_self.w4, t.mbar_all.w4, t.mbar_self.w8), T_i = hardware sample total per iteration of (a), k_i = SYNCS instructions per iteration on the SM = 2 x warps. h100 (47.24 x 8 + 51.09 x 8 + 86.87 x 16) / 384 = 5.67; b300 (49.92 x 8 + 50.95 x 8 + 85.96 x 16) / 384 = 5.68. Evidence measured; sources sync_basic.h100.v2 / sync_basic.b300.v2.
leaves.control.nanosleep.cycles: points (request ns, cycles) = the clock cost per sleep of the one-warp cells (derive column 'cost', launch 2): h100 (100, 244.35) (1000, 2024.14) (10000, 31999.47) (100000, 254192.25) (1000000, 1881736.06); b300 (100, 249.33) (1000, 2064.23) (10000, 32622.53) (100000, 243709.00) (1000000, 1944673.03); and a point at 0 on the line through the first two (h100 46.60, b300 47.67) so that requests below 100 ns follow the short law instead of the 100 ns value. The table clamps above 1 ms (the PTX cap). Between 1 us and 10 us the two regimes meet at an unmeasured request: interpolation there is not evidence (no such request in either full-GPU set). Evidence measured; same sources.
leaves.unchanged: synchronization.mbarrier.release.cycles / suspended_wake_cycles, instruction.service SYNCS.PHASECHK, synchronization.cta.release, control.nanosleep.syncs_wake_cycles.

replay: The version 1 and version 2 cells of both devices are replayed from their existing captures with the new formal build (clean clone, seven gates) into $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/sync_basic-v3/<device>; hardware columns are the existing reference passes. Numbers are cycles per loop iteration (sum over the loop-body pcs of the ledger), as in (a).

criteria.C1 (R1): s.mbar_self and t.mbar_all at one warp per CTA: replay total within 15 % of the hardware sample total (h100 27.68 / 27.99, b300 27.24 / 27.56); semantic:mbarrier_wait on the try_wait pcs at most 1 cycle per iteration; the wait sits on the readers of the try_wait predicates (barrier:SYNCS.PHASECHK) and is within 25 % of the hardware long_scoreboard there (16.96 / 18.31, 17.03 / 18.21).
criteria.C2 (R2): t.mbar_self.w2, s.mbar_self.w4, t.mbar_all.w4, t.mbar_self.w8: replay total within 15 % of the hardware sample total (h100 32.96 / 47.24 / 51.09 / 86.87, b300 31.27 / 49.92 / 50.95 / 85.96), the wait on the readers as in C1 (the hardware's mio_throttle share on the SYNCS at 8 warps is reported as not modelled).
criteria.C3 (untouched cells): s.loop*, s.bar*, s.membar*, s.mbar_trywait_fail*: ledger and cycles identical to the 74ce8aab replay. s.mbar_arrive*: total within 1 cycle per iteration of the 74ce8aab replay (the arrives take turns at the server but nothing waits on them). t.mbar_pingpong (one pair): within 3 cycles per iteration of the 74ce8aab replay (a SYNCS issued within one interval of the other warp's is served after it; nothing else of another warp's wait changes); t.mbar_pingpong.w8 (four pairs on the server) is reported.
criteria.C4 (R3): s.sleep100, s.sleep1000 (1 and 4 warps), t.sleep10u, t.sleep100u, t.sleep1m: replay cycles per sleep within 3 % of the hardware clock cost (these are the points themselves; the check is that the request reaches the leaf in the unit the table is stated in); the wait stays where it is (suspended:sleep after the NANOSLEEP).
criteria.decision: C1 failing on either device: R1 is not installed. C2 failing on a device: that device's service_interval_cycles stays 0 and the readings are reported. C4 failing on a device: that device keeps its old leaf. C3 failing: the cause is found before anything is installed. Criteria are not changed after the replays; a failed one is reported with its numbers.

full_gpu: After installation both 500-case sets are replayed with ledgers and compared (attribution, site and per-pc errors, MAPE) for the table of stall-attribution.md section 4. Reported, not a criterion. Hypotheses, not expectations to be met: cases with plain NANOSLEEP (mostly b300) lose replay time at those sites; elsewhere little moves, because full-GPU mbarrier waits are waits on another warp or on TMA, which this version does not touch.
not_installed_here: The hand-off between two warps (pending try_wait, hint form / NANOSLEEP.SYNCS, a wait issued after another warp's arrive), bar.sync, the 1.96 microsecond try_wait time-out (replay folds failed polls), arrive behind a lane-predicate branch (17-21 against 37-40: the difference is the control floor the replay puts behind BSSY, a matter of the branch step), the bounded SYNCS queue (mio_throttle).
not_allowed: No value from another machine or from the literature; no full-GPU case used to choose a rule or a value.

addenda.when: 2026-11-17, before any engine change or replay under this version
addenda.text: Not executed as written. Version 4's readings (its addendum) arrived before the implementation started and show that R1 holds for every warp, not only the one that completed the phase (a try_wait issued after another warp's arrive, and one blocked when it comes, both return one result latency after the later of the two; no release latency, no wake cost). Installing R1 for the own warp alone would add a special case that the next version removes. Version 5 therefore carries R2 and R3 word for word with their leaves and criteria C1-C4, and replaces R1 by the general rule; no replay was made under version 3 and no criterion of it was judged or changed after data.
